name: Sticker-Style Explainer Animation
visualIdentity: Scientific objects and symbols appear as consistent stickers with rounded silhouettes, clean white borders, light shadows, and stable colors or symbols for each concept. Short labels and purposeful arrows connect a question, objects, mechanism, and conclusion. This is practical prompt guidance, not an established art movement.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to explanatory and illustrated narratives; it can stand alone for concept walkthroughs. Suggested for science, health, or climate explanations with a few key figures, classroom lessons, and short social science explainers. Interactive HTML can reveal notes by step, update charts, or support card sorting. These are suggested fits, not guarantees.
limitations: Decoration must not obscure explanations; chart marks stay flat and border-free, and bouncing chart marks can distort readings. Keep notes to one per step, use arrows for causality only, and prevent notes or peel motion from competing with labels. Do not force chapter transitions onto short topics or let transitions obscure causality, break continuous-shot or loop requirements, or replace explanation with spectacle. Avoid clutter, invented data, and unverified geographic meaning.
palette: Suggested only for new artwork when no task, brand, reference, or existing semantic colors are approved: background #F5EFDF; foreground #2C424D; white #FFFFFF for consistent sticker borders, not another concept category; teal #73A59E and warm #D28C67 as accents. Five authored suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve supplied colors, role assignments, families, and limits; do not auto-recolor, expand hues, or add gradients. Keep one dominant background and clear hierarchy. Foreground on background is reported at 9.177 contrast; white on foreground at 10.534. Text on teal (3.815) or warm accent (3.856) misses the 4.5 normal-text target, so use these as decorative fills and put body copy on an existing contrasting backing. Recheck actual composited frames; two-color ratios do not establish full accessibility.
motionAndInteraction: Use purposeful placing, peeling, path movement, and restrained bounce; reveal relationships in explanatory order and preserve reading holds. Pan and scale scene containers rather than using an enormous bitmap. Motion references are optional: chapter handoffs or progress-led storytelling fit only where scenes and narrative support them; choose one transition treatment and coherent forward, backward, and direct-seek states. For HTML, scroll may drive finite narrative states, and hover, pointer, or drag behavior is interactive-only; provide keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion access as applicable. Dragula may support card sorting with stable IDs, persisted state, alternatives, and cleanup. Video must derive state from seekable composition time, not live input. Give each animated property one owner and verify arbitrary seeks.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject, audience, story, and explicit audio requirements. State assumptions; do not assume assets exist. Synchronize picture and sound, leave room for comprehension, and check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Use accurate, consistent scientific objects, symbols, short labels, arrows, charts, and transparent sticker artwork in a shared scene coordinate system. Preserve exact copy, source artwork, and stable concept mappings. Load local fonts and assets before rendering. Optional tldraw can author editable diagrams or annotations but is not a renderer; D3 can calculate chart scales and paths; SVG draws scalable marks. Cytoscape.js suits node-edge concepts with validated IDs and cached layouts; Leaflet suits real geography with verified coordinates, authorized map assets, and attribution. Add accessible text or table context for interactive graphs and maps. Optional Rough.js can make seeded sketch contours, not handwriting or authentic drawing materials.
combinations: Pairs well with style-097 charts for science, health, or climate explainers: charts remain accurate and flat without sticker borders, concept stickers retain stable colors, and labels or axes stay unobscured; HTML can provide a stepper and accessible data table. Style-024 handwritten annotations can link mechanism steps: keep notes foreground-colored, one per step, arrows causal, and notes secondary to labels, with an accessible transcript in HTML. These are recommendations, not requirements.
productionApproach: Choose visual rendering and motion tools for the style and action before the export pipeline; use only needed libraries and document their roles. SVG is a core renderer; PixiJS, D3, tldraw, Cytoscape.js, Leaflet, and seeded Rough.js are optional for their specific 2D, chart, authoring, graph, map, or contour capabilities. GSAP is the paused, seekable timeline contract; Motion, mo.js, or Anime.js are optional only with verified time synchronization and separate property ownership. HyperFrames is primary for assembly, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export; Remotion is allowed only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with the reason recorded. Neither defines the visual method. For interactive HTML, use suitable live interaction adapters; for video, make all states deterministic and seekable. Audio is chosen separately, then synchronized and mixed through the selected pipeline.
